verifications.claim: As of early April 2, 2026, the Artemis II crew is in a high-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 7:54 AM / April 2, 2026 Artemis II crew begins first day in space... The crew is spending about 24 hours orbiting the Earth... 8:52 PM / April 1, 2026... raising the high point, or apogee, of the orbit to 43,760 miles... highly elliptical 24-hour-long orbit
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states the crew is orbiting Earth in a highly elliptical high-Earth orbit as of early April 2, matching the claim precisely.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew launched successfully from Kennedy Space Center on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:36 PM / April 1, 2026 Artemis II lifts off... from the Kennedy Space Center'; R3: '6:35 pm ET April 1, 2026Artemis II liftoff!... Kennedy Space Center'; R5: 'At 6:35 p.m. EDT... lifted off from the Kennedy Space Center'; R6: 'Launch dateApril 1, 2026... Launch siteKennedy, LC-39B'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm successful launch from Kennedy Space Center on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is conducting systems tests.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 7:54 AM / April 2... put their Orion capsule through its paces... check out the Orion capsule, making sure the ship's communications, navigation, propulsion and life support systems are working properly before heading to the moon.
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly describes ongoing systems tests on Orion capsule post-launch.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is preparing for a translunar injection burn to head toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The crew will spend their first 24 hours or so in orbit around the Earth doing checks... Then... 'trans-lunar injection,' or TLI, will boost them on a path to the moon.
verifications.reasoning: R1 details preparation in orbit for the upcoming TLI burn to head to the Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is currently safe in orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '9:45 PM... the ascent was an "amazing ride,"'; R3: '8:19 pm ET April 1, 2026... The crew is doing well and safely in orbit.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm crew is safe and well in orbit shortly after launch.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; exact match in others.
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew list confirmed across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.'; R3: '6:35 pm ET April 1, 2026Artemis II liftoff!'; R5: 'At 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R6: 'April 1, 2026, 22:35:12 UTC (6:35:12 p.m. EDT)'
verifications.reasoning: Precise time and date match across sources.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is nicknamed Integrity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The Orion spacecraft — nicknamed “Integrity” by the crew'; R5: 'Orion spacecraft, named Integrity'; R6: 'Orion CM-003 Integrity'

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule is in an elliptical high-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: highly elliptical 24-hour-long orbit... apogee to 43,760 miles
verifications.reasoning: R1 describes exact orbit type post-launch.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule has separated from the interim cryogenic propulsion stage (ICPS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 10:01 PM / April 1, 2026 Orion separates from interim cryogenic propulsion stage... 11:40 PM... separation from the detached ICPS upper stage.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will remain in high-Earth orbit to test systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: spending about 24 hours orbiting the Earth while they put their Orion capsule through its paces... giving them plenty of time to check out the Orion capsule
verifications.reasoning: R1 states they remain in orbit for ~24 hours to test systems.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will execute a burn to travel toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'trans-lunar injection,' or TLI, will boost them on a path to the moon'; R2: 'successfully conducting the translunar injection burn'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm planned and executed TLI burn to Moon.

verifications.claim: The burn will start a 10-day round trip.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'From launch... to splashdown on April 10, the mission is slated to last about nine and a half days'; R2: '10 days'; R6: '9 days, 1 hour'
verifications.reasoning: Mission duration ~9-10 days total; burn starts lunar leg, but claim approximates as '10-day round trip' without precise distinction.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight to the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R4: 'first time since 1972 during Apollo 17'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: Artemis II serves as a test for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'thoroughly test their Orion capsule... to make sure it's up to the task'; R6: 'test flight supporting subsequent Artemis missions aimed at returning humans to the lunar surface'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it as test mission for future lunar operations including landings.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is expected to last roughly 9-10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'nine and a half days'; R2: '10 days'; R6: '9 days, 1 hour'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is expected to conclude with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown on April 10'; R6: 'Landing sitePacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify splashdown in Pacific Ocean.
